properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked with the root-cause skill, measured): add_decision and add_requirement answered "does this call need the owner's name?" and "is the given status written?" with ONE boolean, the settle table's. When #635 (2026-09-29) narrowed the Decision row to the statuses that decide, rejected and superseded stopped being written, silently, while the approver signature was drawn unconditionally
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL (root-cause, fetched fresh through the hub), 2026-10-19, for fact:add-decision-given-status-rejected-and-an-approver-writes-proposed-and-says-nothing-2026-10-18.

① OBSERVED: add_decision with an approver stored accepted/deferred as given and rejected/superseded as `proposed`, AUTHORED_BY role=approver drawn all the same; the loop hint said "a Decision lands `proposed`". NOT affected: set_decision_status rejected; add_requirement's statuses on create.

② PRECEDENT: fact:root-cause-add-decisions-lands-proposed-hint-recurred-on-the-one-call-settle-path-2026-09-29 (the hint, a different symptom, fixed by #623). No record of this one.

③ CANDIDATES: (a) the handler writes the status only when the call settles; (b) the core set_decision_status refuses or rewrites retiring statuses; (c) something after the write (keep_the_choice, the review) resets status; (d) the observation is wrong.

④⑤ MEASURED on main 6a45d4b: a class test walking all nine constructors that take `status`, every schema value, create and revise, with and without approver (tests/a_constructor_stores_the_status_it_was_given.rs). 5 of 5 failed. Findings: add_decision rejected/superseded land `proposed` with AND without an approver (so the 10-18 note that the unsigned call "is refused" did not reproduce: it is stored `proposed` silently too); a revise to `proposed` over a settled Decision OR Requirement is ignored; an approver with no status, or with `proposed`, is drawn on a `proposed` node; an unknown Decision status lands `proposed` without a word. The seven constructors with no approver store every value. (b) refuted: set_decision_status stores rejected. (c) refuted: the status was never written — capture.rs `if settles { set_decision_status(..) }`, and `settles` = crate::settles::rule("add_decision") = In(accepted, deferred, contested). (a) confirmed.

⑥ CLASS: two questions answered by one value. #440 (2026-09-06) wrote `if settles {write}` when settles meant "status != proposed", so the two coincided; #635 (2026-09-29) narrowed the Decision row so an unsigned `rejected` was no longer refused, and the write narrowed with it. sign_as_approver never asked what was stored. add_requirement was right only because its row still reads NotIn(proposed), and shared the revise-to-proposed hole.

⑦ PINNED: the class test above, observed failing first on main (5 of 5), green after.

⑧ FIX (corrected_cause): both constructors store exactly the status given (create and revise); the settle gate only decides whether a name is needed; `approver` with no status or with `proposed` is refused (nothing to sign); an unknown status is refused before the create (capture.rs approver_signs_a_stored_status).

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED: the generic create_node/create_nodes sign only a settling status and drop an approver on any other without a word — not changed here. Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019Xbw6PG9mXJiU2Sb421fnq
